text:
sara_support: Hey team, incoming escalation from AcmeCorp. They say embeddings from our hosted API vs their Dedicated pool are not matching — dims and similarity scores differ. Customer noticed this after migrating some traffic to Dedicated yesterday.

sara_support: Summary from customer: hosted returns 512-d vectors, Dedicated returns 768-d. They included identical input text, same API key (scoped), and same model name `open-embed-medium-v1`. They also saw higher tail latency on Dedicated for batched requests. Customer says this is breaking downstream nearest-neighbor indexing.

sara_support: Customer provided curl repro. Pasting sanitized snippet: 
```bash
# hosted (works as expected)
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-medium-v1","input":"acme product launch Q1"}'

# response vector length: 512
```

```bash
# dedicated endpoint (different result)
curl -s -X POST https://dedicated-us.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ded-***' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-medium-v1","input":"acme product launch Q1"}'

# response vector length: 768
```

sara_support: They also attached a small CSV of 20 rows where cosine similarity between hosted and dedicated embeddings is ~0.4-0.6 (should be ~0.98). They flagged severity P1 because their search results broke on production index update.

mike_eng: @sara_support thanks for the triage. First thought: model artifact mismatch or different model config/quantization in Dedicated. Even if the model name is same, the dedicated pool can point to a different model bundle or a converted artifact.

mike_eng: Can we ask customer to `GET /v1/models/open-embed-medium-v1` on both endpoints and paste the model `version`/`artifact_id`? That will tell us if they are actually hitting different variants.

sara_support: Asked customer to run the GET. They returned: hosted -> version `2025-02-11-a1`; dedicated -> version `2025-02-11-a1` (same). So they claim identical version metadata.

leo_runtime: Hmm. If versions match, possibilities: (1) runtime kernel/quantization pipeline on Dedicated differs (different build flags), (2) request path is being routed to a fallback model variant (e.g., `open-embed-medium-v1-quant`), or (3) vector post-processing (padding/truncation or concatenation) is applied somewhere.

leo_runtime: Can we get the raw embedding length and a hex of the first 8 floats (or base64) from both endpoints? That will let us see if dims are appended or padded. Also need request headers for both calls (X-Deployment-Node, X-Model-Variant).

jordan_cs: Customer sent headers for both calls. Hosted has `X-Backend-Node: host-23`, `X-Model-Variant: canonical`. Dedicated shows `X-Backend-Node: ded-5`, `X-Model-Variant: canonical-quant`. They didn't think the suffix mattered.

mike_eng: The suffix matters a lot. `canonical-quant` can be a quantized artifact with different output geometry if artifact conversion was accidentally concatenating provenance vectors (weird but not impossible). @leo_runtime can you check the model manifest for `canonical-quant`?

leo_runtime: Looking up manifests. Quick check: dedicated artifact `canonical-quant` has `output_dim: 768` in its manifest. canonical has `output_dim: 512`. That matches customer observation. Why is Dedicated routing to `canonical-quant` when they requested `canonical`? Need to check routing policy for that Dedicated pool.

mike_eng: Good catch. Two follow-ups: (1) check that the Dedicated pool config doesn't have a model override mapping (we had a recent rollout that added `fallback_variants` config for quantized fallbacks); (2) confirm the customer's dedicated deployment image hasn't inadvertently pulled a newer manifest with wrong mapping.

sara_support: I pinged @deploy-bot to show recent deploys to the Dedicated cluster for that customer.

deploy-bot: Recent actions for dedicated-acme: 
- 2026-01-22T18:02:13Z deploy config update (operator: infra-oncall)
- 2026-01-22T18:02:17Z model mapping change: added fallback `canonical -> canonical-quant` (operator: infra-oncall)

sara_support: Ohhh. That mapping change looks suspicious. Customer said migration happened yesterday and mapping change timestamp aligns.

tasha_ml: If their requests are being routed to `canonical-quant`, that explains output dim change and potential quality differences. Quantized variant often reduces cosine similarity to canonical floats. It shouldn't change output_dim but here it did because quant variant was built from a different checkpoint (bad build). We need to rollback mapping or rebuild `canonical-quant` to match dims.

leo_runtime: Next steps I propose: 
1) Immediate mitigation: add a temporary routing fix to prioritize `canonical` for acme's dedicated pool. I can push a rollback in a few minutes if infra approves.
2) Run hermetic repro: our eng will hit both endpoints with identical payloads, capture model variant headers, and vector lengths for 100 samples.
3) Postmortem: find why `canonical-quant` was built from wrong checkpoint and why mapping was applied cluster-wide.

mike_eng: Also important for debugging: test with batching. Customer reported large batch requests (batch_size=64) on Dedicated had massive tail latency. That could be the quant op kernel not supporting efficient batching. Let's repro with `batch_size=1` and `batch_size=64` and compare 95th percentile latency.

sara_support: Customer accepted mitigation. They've unpaused index updates for now but want us to confirm no other customers are affected.

jordan_cs: I notified the customer that we're rolling a targeted fix and will follow up with timeline. They asked for ETA <= 2 hours.

leo_runtime: I'm starting the routing override now (scoped to acme dedicated pool). Will report back when live.

leo_runtime: override applied at 1780432150. Verified traffic to ded-5 now reports `X-Model-Variant: canonical` and response vectors are length 512 for the same sample.

sara_support: Confirmed with customer — they ran their small CSV again. Cosine similarity is back to ~0.98 and search results restored. They are happy for now but want a root cause analysis.

mike_eng: Assigning action items: 
- @tasha_ml to own artifact rebuild and verification test (ensure `canonical-quant` built from same checkpoint and `output_dim`=512).
- @leo_runtime to audit routing policy change (who approved fallback and scope).
- @mike_eng to run perf tests comparing quant vs canonical at batch sizes [1,8,32,64] and produce numbers.

tasha_ml: I'll run artifact rebuild and add CI check for `manifest.output_dim` matching canonical. Also adding a pre-merge check to prevent fallback mapping for a variant with different output_dim.

sara_support: Thanks all. Customer wants closure note and postmortem within 48 hours. I'll keep the thread updated and coordinate the PMR.

mike_eng: Great triage everyone. Logging this for postmortem: root cause likely human config change + bad quant artifact build. Temporary routing override restored parity and reduced latency.

sara_support: Closing loop for now. I'll add the detailed logs and full repro commands to the support ticket.

jordan_cs: Marking resolved on customer ticket pending postmortem. :white_check_mark:

leo_runtime: Follow-ups will be tracked in #eng-runtime postmortem thread.

sara_support: End of thread.
